subject: Information Theory
title: Golay Codes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Golay Codes.

hook.text: In 1949, Marcel Golay published a half-page paper describing a perfect code. It's been used in spacecraft ever since.

buildup.text: The binary Golay code (23,12) encodes 12 data bits into 23 bits and corrects any combination of up to 3 errors.

discovery.text: It's a perfect code: every possible received word is within distance 3 of exactly one codeword. No decoding ambiguity.

twist.text: Perfect codes are extremely rare. The only nontrivial binary perfect codes are Hamming codes and the Golay code.

climax.text: The Golay code was used in the Voyager missions and connects to the Leech lattice in pure mathematics.

punchline.text: A half-page paper. A perfect code. Used in deep space.

quiz.question: What makes the Golay code special?
options: It is one of the few perfect binary error-correcting codes
